body: ## Pull request overview This PR fixes ghost dependency issues by clearing undo history when resources referenced in AnimationPlayer keyframes are deleted from the file system. The implementation connects to the `FileSystemDock::file_removed` signal and clears the undo history for affected animations to release stale resource references. **Key Changes:** - Added `_file_removed` handler to AnimationPlayerEditorPlugin that triggers when files are deleted - Clears undo history for the current animation and AnimationTrackEditor when resource files are removed - Detects resource file types via hardcoded file extension list ### Reviewed changes Copilot reviewed 2 out of 2 changed files in this pull request and generated 4 comments. | File | Description | | ---- | ----------- | | editor/animation/animation_player_editor_plugin.h | Declares the new `_file_removed` method handler | | editor/animation/animation_player_editor_plugin.cpp | Implements connection to `file_removed` signal and handler that clears undo history when resource files are deleted | --- 💡 Add Copilot custom instructions for smarter, more guided reviews. Learn how to get started.

I think this is the wrong way to fix it.

The ghosting issue with undo fundamentally doesn't depend on the AnimationPlayerEditor. If you remove the AnimationPlayer in your MRP, and directly swap the Sprite2D texture, and delete previous texture and performing undo, ghosting should still appear there.

Therefore, handling undoredo solely within the AnimationPlayerEditor is at least misguided. If you want to eliminate ghosting, a fundamental implementation change is likely required.

As pointed out in https://github.com/godotengine/godot/issues/114637#issuecomment-3717364226, I think adding some cleanup to AnimationPlayerEditor when closing Godot is the right approach, but this PR is currently doing the wrong thing.
